title: Personal branding isn't product branding
author: Josue Valles
summary: Josue Valles argues that personal branding fails when treated like product branding, because a person is dynamic and a product is static. He replaces the sterile positioning statement with a three-tense story: the Then, the Now and the Future. Writers tend to get stuck in one tense, whether the resume-like past, the tip-heavy present or the visionary future. He says authority comes from the overlap of past and present, and connection from the overlap of present and future. The same topics, such as people, tools and beliefs, can appear in every tense. His practical advice is simply to notice which tense a post is in and reach a little into the others.
points: Valles says a personal brand should be dynamic and authentic rather than a formulaic positioning statement.
He frames a brand as three tenses: the Then, the Now and the Future.
Writing stuck only in the past reads like a resume, only in the present lacks story, and only in the future lacks belief.
Authority comes from linking past to present, and connection from linking present to future.
The same topics can be written in all three tenses, so the approach is easier than it sounds.
quotes: A lot of people approach personal branding like product branding.
The overlap between your past and present is where authority comes from.
The overlap between your present and future is where connection comes from.
People like to join something that's moving, and they like to feel they were there early.
In the past tense, you can write about the mentors who shaped you.
Next time you write something, just notice which tense you're in, and ask yourself whether the post would be stronger if it reached a little into the past or a little into the future.
